sentences.text: Scientists know this animal from only two skeletons.
One of these is an almost complete skeleton now held by the Royal Ontario Museum.
This larger individual measured about 7 meters long with a skull reaching 1.54 meters.
The other specimen was much smaller, with a skull of 0.785 meters and a body of nearly 4 meters, showing it was a juvenile.
Christopher McGowan first described Excalibosaurus in 1986.
An almost complete second specimen was collected in 1996 from the same area and purchased by the Royal Ontario Museum.
McGowan described this second specimen again in 2003.
Excalibosaurus belongs to the family Leptonectidae alongside the genera Leptonectes and Eurhinosaurus.

Although once thought to be a junior synonym of Eurhinosaurus, the 1996 specimen shows morphological differences like a shorter, broader forefin and a slender body that clearly differentiate the two genera.
Excalibosaurus lived during the Sinemurian stage of the Early Jurassic period in what is now England.
Excalibosaurus lived approximately 199.5 to 192.9 million years ago during the Early Jurassic period.
